reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown read Jeremiah as filling a gap Chronicles leaves open, with Nebuchadnezzar killing Jehoiakim en route and leaving him near Jerusalem.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen calls Chronicles' claim that Jehoiakim was fettered and carried to Babylon an impossibility, exposing the very verse the location tension depends on.

quotes.text: the punishment of the godless Jehoiakim is magnified; he is stated to have been put in irons by the Chaldaeans and carried to Babylon (xxxvi. 6)--an impossibility of course before the capture of Jerusalem, which did not take place until the third month of his successor.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), on 2 Chronicles 36:6.

sides.snippet: bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon
sides.verseText: Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.

sides.snippet: cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem
sides.verseText: He shall be buried with the burial of a donkey, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
